punchline: Turning a thermostat to the top does not warm the room faster, because the dial only decides when to stop.
thirty_sec: In Don Norman's book, a thermostat dial and a two-control refrigerator show how a wrong mental picture misleads. People turn the thermostat to the top to heat faster, but the setting only decides when heating shuts off. The fridge's freezer and fresh-food controls are not independent, and a colder freezer can freeze the salad. Norman says the controls suggest a false conceptual model.
